causal_chain: A target-conditioned support selector over historical items can isolate which interactions justify preferring a candidate item for the current user.
More robust support-grounded scoring should improve full-sort NDCG@10 versus static pairwise collaborative filters under the same frozen protocol.

Scoring with both direct user-item affinity and support-aggregated evidence should raise scores for positives that are weak under global preference averages but well supported by a coherent subset of history.
Static user embeddings compress all history into one vector, so pairwise updates can reinforce shortcut co-occurrence rather than target-relevant support evidence.
Training an auxiliary stability objective under removal of selected support items discourages brittle reliance on single shortcut interactions and promotes distributed support representations.
Users often have heterogeneous histories where only a subset of past items actually supports a given target positive.
blind_projection.closest_parent: A recommender that learns which historical interactions most support each positive target and explicitly trains ranking margins to remain stable when those support interactions are removed will generalize better in offline top-n recommendation than a matched model trained only on factual pairwise ranking, because it suppresses brittle shortcut co-occurrence reliance and promotes support-distributed user representations.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any gain could come merely from adding parameters or extra regularization rather than from target-conditioned support attribution and support-removal stability.
discriminative_predictions: Learned support weights should concentrate on different historical items for different candidate targets from the same user rather than behaving like a static user-attention profile.
Removing the support-removal stability term while keeping the same target-conditioned support scorer should reduce robustness and narrow or erase gains on hard positives.

The candidate should outperform a parameter-matched direct-affinity control most clearly for users with longer and more diverse histories, where target-conditioned support selection has room to disambiguate intent.
expected_evidence: Ablation comparing full model versus mechanism-off scorer-only or stability-off variants separates the value of support selection from generic model capacity.
Diagnostics on support-weight entropy and target-specific support overlap indicate whether the model is using adaptive support rather than static history summarization.
Qualification runs show whether the executable descendant beats a matched direct-affinity control on full-sort NDCG@10 under the frozen ML-1M protocol.
blind_projection.falsifier: If the model fails to beat a matched direct-affinity control, or if a mechanism-off variant without target-conditioned support selection and removal-stability performs equivalently, then the hypothesis that support-grounded counterfactual robustness is the useful mechanism is not supported.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This proposal moves beyond all active-profile families by introducing target-conditioned history-to-candidate interaction scoring and an explicit counterfactual support-removal stability loss. It is not a parameter tweak of BPR-MF or LightGCN and requires new per-triplet history encoding, support masking, and auxiliary optimization logic in a candidate-local GeneralRecommender.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A pairwise-trained recommender that scores each candidate through target-conditioned selection of supporting historical items and regularizes the ranking margin to remain stable after removing selected support evidence will improve full-sort NDCG@10 over static collaborative filtering, because it learns which parts of a user's history justify each recommendation and avoids brittle shortcut support.
implementation_requirements: Add an auxiliary counterfactual stability loss by masking one or more top-support historical items for the positive target and penalizing excessive collapse of the positive-negative margin.
Build support summaries as weighted sums of historical item embeddings and combine them with direct user-item affinity in the final pairwise score.
For each training triplet (u, i+, j-), retrieve the user's interacted history from the train split only and compute target-conditioned support weights over history separately for i+ and j-.
Implement a candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender with user and item embeddings plus item-history embeddings indexed from the training interaction matrix.
Provide efficient batching with capped history length or sampled history truncation compatible with the qualification budget while preserving the fixed frozen protocol semantics.
Support full-sort inference by computing each candidate's direct score plus target-conditioned support score from the stored user history without using held-out interactions.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use a matched direct-affinity control with the same embedding dimensionality, optimizer, training schedule, and history access path, but replace target-conditioned support selection with uniform or static pooled history aggregation and remove the support-removal stability loss.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Introduce a target-conditioned support attribution module over each user's training-history items and a counterfactual support-removal stability objective on pairwise margins.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Mechanism-off keeps the same embeddings and history retrieval but replaces target-conditioned support weights with a fixed unconditioned pooled history vector and removes the support-removal stability loss, reducing the model to direct affinity plus static history context.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: Add a target-conditioned history-support scorer on top of direct user-item affinity, then test whether including a support-removal stability loss improves over the same scorer without that loss and over a matched static-history control.
blind_projection.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M full-sort pairwise protocol, does an executable support-attribution recommender with counterfactual support-removal stability outperform matched static collaborative filtering by better identifying which historical interactions justify each target item?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: The candidate is feasible within the qualification budget if user histories are truncated or padded to a fixed maximum length and support masking is limited to one or a few top-support items per triplet; computational cost should remain moderate because ML-1M user histories are manageable and the model uses simple embedding interactions rather than full graph propagation.
